details:
First of all, thank you for bringing VRChat to mobile platforms; it has opened the doors for so many new users.

I would like to propose a feature that could bridge the gap between Flat Mode and Standalone VR for mobile users: An Experimental 3DoF Split-Screen VR Mode.

The Idea:

Allow mobile players to toggle a "VR Mode" that splits the screen into a stereoscopic view (compatible with Google Cardboard or VR Box headsets). This mode would utilize the smartphone’s built-in Gyroscope for 3DoF head tracking (looking around), while relying on a standard Bluetooth Gamepad/Controller for movement, jumping, and menu navigation.

Why this would be amazing:

While we understand that full 6DoF tracking and hand controllers are ideal, millions of users own phone-VR headsets and controllers. Giving them a low-cost entry point to actually "sit inside" VRChat worlds—even in a limited 3DoF capacity—would drastically increase immersion and accessibility for those who cannot afford standalone VR headsets.

Addressing Potential Challenges:

Performance: This could be introduced as an "Experimental Feature" with a clear warning regarding performance and battery heat. It could also be restricted only to "Excellent" or "Good" optimized mobile worlds.

Comfort: A comfort warning about motion sickness (due to mobile latency) can be displayed before enabling the mode.

Thank you for considering this idea to make VRChat even more accessible!

Best regards,

Novel21
title: Optional 3DoF Split-Screen VR Mode for VRChat Mobile (Gyro + Gamepad Support)
